title: Understanding the Scatter Plot
text: The scatter plot shows a negative correlation between age and mpg. As age increases, mpg decreases.

title: Analyzing Plot (a)
text: Plot (a) shows a distribution with multiple peaks. Which variable, age or mpg, is likely to have such a distribution?

title: Analyzing Plot (b)
text: Plot (b) shows a distribution with a single peak. Consider which variable, age or mpg, might have this kind of distribution.

title: Analyzing Plot (c)
text: Plot (c) is a histogram with a uniform distribution. Does this match the distribution of age or mpg?

title: Analyzing Plot (d)
text: Plot (d) shows a histogram with a skewed distribution. Consider which variable, age or mpg, might have this kind of distribution.

title: Analyzing Plot (e.i) and (e.ii)
text: These plots show point plots with confidence intervals. Which variable, age or mpg, do these plots likely represent?

title: Analyzing Plot (f.i) and (f.ii)
text: These plots also show point plots with confidence intervals. Consider which variable, age or mpg, might be represented here.

title: Analyzing Plot (g.i) and (g.ii)
text: These are scatter plots. Compare them with the labeled scatter plot to determine which variable is on each axis.

title: Analyzing Plot (h.i) and (h.ii)
text: These plots show a perfect linear relationship. Consider which variable, age or mpg, might have this kind of relationship.
